items.quote: When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest:
items.claim: The text tells the Israelites that, once they have settled in the promised land and are reaping its harvest, they must bring a sheaf of the first grain harvested to the priest.
items.action: bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of the harvest
items.mechanism: divine command passed on through Moses
items.place: the land which I give unto you

items.quote: And he shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, to be accepted for you:
items.claim: The priest waves the firstfruits sheaf before the LORD, and the text says its purpose is to win acceptance for the people.
items.action: wave the sheaf before the LORD
items.mechanism: wave offering to be accepted on the people's behalf

items.quote: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.
items.claim: The wave offering is set for the day after the sabbath. All three passes agreed on this item. The text does not say which sabbath it means.
items.mechanism: timing set relative to the sabbath

items.quote: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, 23:10 Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them,
items.claim: The text presents the firstfruits law as the LORD's words to Moses, which Moses is to repeat to the Israelites. The document gives only verse numbers (23:9–11). Naming it as Leviticus 23 comes from model-prior and is not verified by the evidence text.
